reviewer_statement: Developer-side source semantic and scientific frame schema review of generalized_function_on_scalar_mean_difference_frame against published eyetrajectoriespy 1.2.0. New native R validation plus original Python typed dataclass oracle fixtures propose 23 complete source result frames across four linked exports and four scientific configurations; all column values, row order and exposure attrs are compared, with malformed R domains tested. Exact-head CI is pending. This does not confer Python object identity or independent certification.
native_language_semantic_policy: Python typed generalized FoSR result dataclasses map to validated R list records, pandas DataFrame maps to R data.frame with identical scientific values and original source order. Python None nullable columns are R typed NA, pandas exposure_audit attrs are R attributes. Native code is Python-free and all source estimands/meaning are preserved.

case_evidence.description: Published frozen Python 1.2 src/eyetrajectoriespy/generalized_function_on_scalar_prediction.py source for typed generalized scientific fit/prediction/band result and native R frame function.
Rate, exposure-adjusted count, nullable exposure units, and binomial fixed-profile source records, each with/without the relevant coefficient/prediction bands; no Python object identity required.

23 direct full-result typed Python source vs native R data.frame tests (all values, exact columns, row order, missing columns and global exposure_audit attributes) across four scientific configurations.

Native R rejects missing/duplicate coefficient IDs, invalid matrix geometry, nonfinite uncertainties, reversed interval limits, invalid exposure, invalid units and scientific metadata mismatches; Python exceptions cannot preserve R class identity.
Source column order, complete row counts, original arbitrary scientific labels, nullable Python None mapped to NA, and source global exposure_audit dictionary mapped to R data.frame attribute.

Predeclared observed-time generalized FoSR profile contrasts, link-vs-response inference scales, pointwise standard errors and simultaneous calibrated lower/upper bands with explicit physical-bound flag.
